instagram:
Paper trade today. My funded account got the day off.

My first entry was wrong. I misread the direction, and the stop took me out: -4 points on 2 ES, -$400.

Then I got short 2 ES at 7,345.25, stop 4 points from entry at 7,349.25.

Price dropped close to 9 points first. Then it climbed all the way back to 7,348.50, three quarters of a point from the stop. I stayed in.

The target at 7,335.00 filled on the next push down: 10.25 points on 2 contracts. The paper day finished about +$625 before fees.

After a stop out, what comes next for you: step away, wait for the next setup, or re-enter?

#MyHobbyismyFREEDOM #definedrisktrading #esfutures #papertrading #daytrading
facebook:
I sat out on my funded account today and traded on paper instead.

It didn't start well. I misread the direction on my first entry and the hard stop took 4 points off both contracts, a $400 paper loss.

Trade two: short 2 ES from 7,345.25, stop 4 points away at 7,349.25, target 7,335.00. Price fell nearly 9 points in my favor, then turned and climbed back to 7,348.50, less than a point from stopping me out.

That stop never filled. Price rolled over again and reached 7,335.00 for 10.25 points on both contracts. Net for the paper session: about +$625 before fees.

Same stop on both trades, 4 points from where I got in.

Have you ever been a tick or two from your stop and still ended up at your target?
